ops.title: Cask-installed daemonkit-based binaries hang pre-main when kernel provenance-tracked (codex-ask, reposync)
ops.description:
On the local machine (Darwin 25.5.0), fresh PATH invocations of the cask-installed codex-ask (1.8.2 AND 1.8.4) and reposync (0.27.4) hang indefinitely pre-main — 0% CPU, zero bytes on stdout/stderr, sample parks at `_dyld_start + 0` — while formula-installed fleet binaries (ccx, cc-notes, slop-cop) run normally.

Controlled probe chain (2026-07-26, identical sha256 6b872393… throughout):
- Caskroom path, quarantine+provenance xattrs → hangs (rc=124)
- /tmp copy, xattrs preserved → hangs
- /tmp copy, `xattr -c` (all cleared) → prints version instantly
- daemonkit-cache materialized copy → runs instantly
- `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` alone on the Caskroom binary → STILL hangs; `com.apple.provenance` survives `xattr -c` (kernel-managed, per-inode)
- fresh-inode copy (cp + xattr -c) swapped over the Caskroom binary → runs instantly; PATH restored for both binaries

Interim fix APPLIED on the local machine: both Caskroom binaries swapped with fresh-inode copies; wedged originals preserved beside them as `*.provenance-wedged` for diagnosis. This recurs on every cask upgrade (brew re-quarantines → first exec re-acquires provenance tracking → wedge).

Open questions / fix directions:
1. Why does kernel provenance tracking block exec indefinitely instead of evaluating? Possibly a wedged syspolicyd/provenance-db state on this machine (a reboot may clear it) — but the binary is notarized and spctl accepts it, so a permanent hang is anomalous regardless.
2. Whether daemonkit's trust-by-codesign / self-materialize startup path contributes (the hang is pre-main, suggesting dyld/AMFI, not Go code — but daemonkit's codeidentity machinery is the common denominator of the two affected binaries alongside cask packaging).
3. Systemic remedy candidates: homebrew-tap cask `postflight` xattr-strip (standard pattern) for every daemonkit-based cask; or ship these as formulae.

Live daemons were unaffected throughout (daemonkit-cache copies are dequarantined) — only fresh PATH invocations wedged, hanging forever instead of erroring, which silently stalls any caller.

ops.text: A fresh cask install/upgrade of codex-ask and reposync executes from PATH without hanging (no manual xattr surgery)
The blocking mechanism is identified and recorded (OS-level provenance anomaly vs daemonkit trust path), with the .provenance-wedged specimens examined or discarded deliberately
